headline: Chips Surge While Software Sinks as Midday Market Splits
body_html:
Stocks are tilting slightly lower at midday Friday, and prices are not yet final. Of the 525 names we track, 243 are higher and 280 are lower, a split that reflects a market sorting winners from losers rather than moving as one.

Semiconductors dominate the tape, up 3.1% as a group and well ahead of every other sector. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor is up 19.97% and Diodes is up 10.97%. The rally is not uniform, though: Microchip is down 13.52%. Energy is the other clear gainer at 1.38%, and materials are up 0.25%. Software is the weakest group at 1.4% lower, with BlackLine down 19.96%. Consumer shares are off 1.14%, healthcare is down 0.83% and homebuilders are down 0.76%.

Into the close, watch whether the chip gains hold and whether the software selling spreads or fades. Crude is also in focus, as Brent is on course for its largest weekly drop since 2020. Traders will also listen for further comment on AI spending before the next session, Monday, November 9.

briefs.headline: Chip Rally Is Real but Uneven
briefs.body: Semiconductors lead all sectors, up 3.1% at midday. Alpha and Omega Semiconductor is up 19.97% and Diodes is up 10.97%. Microchip is down 13.52%, a reminder that the group's strength is concentrated in power and discrete names rather than shared across every chipmaker.

briefs.headline: Networking Gear Catches a Bid
briefs.body: Extreme Networks is up 15.25% and Ubiquiti is up 13.24%. IT reseller ePlus is up 11.29%. The cluster of gains suggests buyers are favoring companies that supply the plumbing of corporate and data-center networks, even as the wider market is split.

briefs.headline: Software Takes the Brunt of the Selling
briefs.body: Software is the worst sector at midday, down 1.4%. BlackLine leads the decliners, off 19.96% and hitting the finance-software corner hardest. The contrast with the chip rally is stark, with money moving toward hardware and away from applications.

briefs.headline: Medical Device Makers Pull in Opposite Directions
briefs.body: Healthcare is down 0.83% overall, yet the device group is volatile. TransMedics is up 18.82%, while Artivion is down 15.67%. The wide gap shows stock-specific news driving prices, not a sector-wide shift in how investors view the industry.

briefs.headline: Energy Gains as Crude Heads for a Weekly Slide
briefs.body: Energy shares are up 1.38%, the second-best sector at midday. That comes as Brent crude is set for its biggest weekly decline since 2020, according to Reuters. Energy equities are holding up despite the weaker oil price, and the close will test that resilience.

briefs.headline: AI Build-Out Talk Meets Sentiment Wobble
briefs.body: Kevin Hassett said the midterm results won't halt data center construction. Meanwhile, betting-market odds of an Anthropic IPO announcement have slipped after the election and the recent AI sell-off. Policy reassurance and market caution are pulling in different directions.
